header: global_seniority_rank is an INTERNAL sort key: grade level x 10,000 + the person's position within that grade. "40,121" means nothing to a reader, so I never let it reach a screen, a table or a CSV. Wherever a list of people carries it, I replace the column -- before anything is displayed or exported -- with what it MEANS: executives -> position_in_grade (the order within the grade is real: earlier in HR's list = more senior) non-executives -> blank (only the GRADE order is meaningful, never the order inside one grade) The rows are still SORTED by the real rank (the SQL does that); only the number is hidden.

symbols.name: addCohortColumn
symbols.sig: export function addCohortColumn( columns: string[], rows: Array<Record<string, any>>, people: PersonLike[] | null | undefined,): { columns: string[]; rows: Array<Record<string, any>> }
doc: I add a "cohort" column (Executive / Non-executive) to a list of people when the SQL did not return one: without it a table or CSV cannot tell the two groups apart (a designation such as "S-9" is not self-explanatory). It goes right after "designation" (else after "name", else last). A person who cannot be identified gets a blank, never a guess.

symbols.name: addDisciplineColumn
symbols.sig: export function addDisciplineColumn( columns: string[], rows: Array<Record<string, any>>, people: PersonLike[] | null | undefined,): { columns: string[]; rows: Array<Record<string, any>> }
doc: I add a "discipline" column (Medicine, ENT ...) to a list of DOCTORS when at least one person in it has a known discipline and the SQL did not return one (step 53a). It goes right after "cohort" (else after "designation", else after "name", else last). A doctor whose discipline is not known gets a blank, never a guess; a list in which nobody has a discipline gets no column at all (a list of non-doctors keeps its columns).

symbols.name: TOTAL_COLUMN
doc: A column that REPEATS the grand total on every row of a list of people ("Total count 16") is noise on a card and on a table row (the headline says it), so I remove it. I touch only a list with a ticket column, at least two rows, a name like total / count / cnt / ..._count and ONE value in every row; a count that differs per row is never touched.

doc: Here I do everything a list of people needs before it is shown or exported: no internal rank, and a cohort column.

symbols.name: withCohortInHint
symbols.sig: export function withCohortInHint(hint: unknown, columns: string[]): unknown
doc: When the model lists the columns it wants (a display hint), that order wins and any column it did not mention is added at the END. The cohort column is added by the system, so it would always land last. I slip it into the hint right after "designation" (else after "name"), where it reads naturally. A hint that already mentions cohort, or names neither, is untouched.
